children: As compared to the third quarter of 2025:
Net income attributable to Oceaneering decreased 26% to $52.6 million.
Cash flow provided by operating activities was $163 million.
Quarter-end cash and cash equivalents totaled $735 million, compared to $506 million at the end of the same period last year.
Shares repurchased were 101,038 for approximately $5.0 million.

Rod Larson, Oceaneering's President and Chief Executive Officer, commented, “Our third-quarter results were in line with our guidance and consensus estimates. Subsea Robotics (SSR) delivered improved year-over-year results, while Offshore Projects Group (OPG) continued to perform well. We generated significant free cash flow during the quarter as a result of improved operational cash and lower tax payments and capital spend. We expect free cash flow generation to moderate in the fourth quarter, but we remain on track to achieve the top end of our full-year guidance.

“As we look ahead, we expect to see typical seasonality and changes in geographic and project mix in the fourth quarter. Beyond the fourth quarter, we expect improved performance in 2027, with EBITDA increasing compared to 2026.

“Third-quarter bookings included meaningful awards across SSR, Manufactured Products, and Aerospace and Defense Technologies (ADTech). Together with our existing backlog and sales opportunities across our businesses, this provides a solid foundation as we enter 2027. Based on our current expectations, we are initiating full-year 2027 EBITDA guidance in the range of $430 million to $480 million.”
As compared to the third quarter of 2025:

SSR revenue increased to $233 million, operating income rose 16% to $75.4 million, and EBITDA margin expanded to 39%. Higher ROV revenue per day utilized, increased Survey activity, and improved margins in ROV operations and in Survey contributed to the year-over-year improvements. ROV revenue per day utilized increased to $11,781, while ROV fleet utilization remained at 65%. Increased ROV activity in Europe, Guyana, and West Africa largely offset lower activity in the U.S. Gulf.

Manufactured Products revenue increased 8%, while operating income was relatively flat at $25.1 million and margin decreased to 15%. Umbilical manufacturing activity was relatively stable compared with the prior year. Increased revenue was primarily attributable to the final resolution of a legacy mobility solutions contract, while lower activity and profitability in Grayloc Products affected operating results. As of September 30, 2026, backlog was $435 million. The book-to-bill ratio was 0.77 for the 12-month period ending on September 30, 2026.

OPG revenue, operating income, and margin remained relatively flat. Results benefited from a favorable mix of installation projects, which more than offset lower activity in West Africa and a less favorable project mix in the U.S. Gulf.

Integrity Management and Digital Solutions (IMDS) revenue increased 7% while operating income was relatively flat. Increased activity in the Middle East, Europe, and the U.S. Gulf was partially offset by lower activity in West Africa, a shift in project mix, and increased costs in the Middle East.

ADTech revenue increased 7% to $135 million, operating income decreased to $14.7 million, and margin declined to 11%. The lower operating results reflect increases in pass-through activities and certain program costs.
At the corporate level, Unallocated Expenses increased to $50.0 million, consistent with expectations.
As compared to the fourth quarter of 2025:
Consolidated fourth quarter 2026 revenue is expected to increase and EBITDA is expected to be in the range of $85 million to $95 million.
At the segment level, for the fourth quarter of 2026:

SSR revenue is expected to increase and operating income is expected to decrease, reflecting lower ROV utilization as certain rigs transit from the U.S. Gulf to other regions, a shift in ROV geographic mix, and increased mobilization costs.
Manufactured Products revenue and operating income are expected to increase.
OPG revenue is expected to remain relatively flat and operating income is expected to decrease on changes in project mix.
IMDS revenue and operating income are expected to increase.
ADTech revenue and operating income are expected to increase.
Unallocated Expenses are expected to be in the $50 million range.
Consolidated EBITDA is expected to be in the range of $430 million to $480 million.
Free cash flow generation is expected to exceed the level forecasted for 2026.
Share repurchase activity is expected to continue.
Oceaneering will provide more specific guidance on its expectations for 2027 in its fourth quarter 2026 earnings release and conference call.

During the third quarter, Oceaneering completed a series of financing transactions that strengthened its capital structure, including the issuance of $500 million aggregate principal amount of 6.875% Senior Notes due 2034 and the amendment and extension of its revolving credit facility, which increased commitments to $345 million and extended maturity to July 2031. These actions significantly extended Oceaneering's debt maturity profile, reduced refinancing risk, and enhanced long-term financial flexibility. As of September 30, 2026, Oceaneering held approximately $735 million of cash and, together with available borrowing capacity under its revolving credit facility, had more than $1.0 billion of liquidity to support ongoing operations, strategic investments, and future growth initiatives.

Adjusted net income (loss) and earnings (loss) per share; EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA on a consolidated and on a segment basis (as well as EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margins); and free cash flow are non-GAAP measures that exclude the impacts of certain identified items. These tables are included below under the caption Reconciliations of Non-GAAP to GAAP Financial Information.

Oceaneering has scheduled a conference call and webcast on Thursday, October 22, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. Central Time (11:00 a.m. Eastern Time), to discuss its results for the third quarter of 2026, guidance for the fourth quarter of 2026, and initial guidance for the full year of 2027. A link to the webcast is posted on Oceaneering's Investor Relations website. A replay of the conference call will be made available on the website approximately two hours following the conclusion of the live call.

RECONCILIATIONS OF NON-GAAP TO GAAP FINANCIAL INFORMATION

In addition to financial results determined in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles ("GAAP"), this press release also includes non-GAAP financial measures (as defined under certain rules and regulations promulgated by the Securities and Exchange Commission). We have included adjusted net income (loss) and diluted earnings (loss) per share (EPS), each of which excludes the effects of certain specified items, as set forth in the tables that follow. As a result, these amounts are non-GAAP financial measures. We believe these are useful measures for investors to review because they provide consistent measures of the underlying results of our ongoing business. Furthermore, our management uses these measures as measures of the performance of our operations. We have also included disclosures of earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA), EBITDA margins, 2025 consolidated adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow, third quarter of 2026 consolidated adjusted EBITDA, consolidated adjusted EBITDA margins, and free cash flow, fourth quarter of 2026 consolidated EBITDA estimate, full year 2026 free cash flow estimate, and full year 2027 consolidated EBITDA estimate, as well as the following by segment: EBITDA, EBITDA margins, adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EBITDA margins. We define EBITDA margin as EBITDA divided by revenue. Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margins and related information by segment exclude the effects of certain specified items, as set forth in the tables that follow. Due to the forward-looking nature of EBITDA for the fourth quarter and full year of 2026 and for the full year of 2027, we cannot reliably predict certain of the necessary line items for the reconciliations to net income and, accordingly, have excluded such line items in the reconciliation. EBITDA and EBITDA margins, adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margins, and related information by segment are each non-GAAP financial measures. We define free cash flow as cash flow provided by operating activities less organic capital expenditures (

., purchases of property and equipment other than those in business acquisitions). We have included these disclosures in this press release because EBITDA, EBITDA margins, and free cash flow are widely used by investors for valuation purposes and for comparing our financial performance with the performance of other companies in our industry, and the adjusted amounts thereof provide more consistent measures than the unadjusted amounts. Furthermore, our management uses these measures for purposes of evaluating our financial performance. Our presentation of EBITDA, EBITDA margins, and free cash flow (and the adjusted amounts thereof) may not be comparable to similarly titled measures that other companies report. Non-GAAP financial measures should be viewed in addition to and not as substitutes for our reported operating results, cash flows, or any other measure prepared and reported in accordance with GAAP.
